source_text.body:
Run a personal agent for servers, accounting, contracts and research
A homegrown agent reachable via Telegram, WhatsApp and email patched servers, sent invoices to an accountant, handled service providers, reviewed contracts and drafted a GDPR request.
·
Nov 18, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The commenter runs a homegrown agent that they reach through Telegram, WhatsApp, email or the command line. In one week it patched their Linux servers for a new nginx vulnerability, replied to their accountant with the invoices requested, took over conversations with service providers, reviewed contracts and fixed typos and wrong dates, and drafted a GDPR request.
How it went
It got a compliance certificate that had been pending for weeks and deflected a provider's repeated taxi-booking messages. It also produced a balanced research report on a tweet about EU sanctions on journalists. The source gives no further numbers or failures.
Worth knowing
The source is a brief comment with no setup details, costs or failure cases; the author describes it as a self-built agent on a VPS with coding agent subscriptions.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Act as my personal admin agent, reachable by [Telegram/WhatsApp/email]. Help with [tasks: server patching, forwarding invoices to my accountant, reviewing a contract, drafting a GDPR request to company] and report back with a short summary of what you did for each task. Before you send any message, run commands on my servers, or pay or delete anything, show me exactly what you plan to do and wait for my OK.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50552924
